Install packages in a Conda environment

Source: R/install_packages.R
install_packages.Rd

Installs packages into an existing environment, from package specs or from an environment file given by env_definition(). install_packages() creates the default environment "condathis-env", empty, when it does not exist. Any other environment that does not exist aborts with class condathis_install_packages_env_not_found (also condathis_env_not_found). Create it with create_env() first.

Usage

install_packages(
  ...,
  env_name = "condathis-env",
  method = "auto",
  verbose = c("output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner", "full"),
  channels = "conda-forge",
  additional_channels = NULL,
  channel_priority = c("strict", "flexible", "disabled")
)

Arguments

...

Package match specs (MatchSpec strings) to install, unnamed: character strings or character vectors, in order. Examples: "python=3.13", "bioconda::samtools". At least one spec is required.

Or one environment file that is solved, given by env_definition(), such as env_definition("environment.yml") or a list of specs, without package specs. Its packages are installed into the environment, solved with the packages it has. With micromamba, this is micromamba install -f <file>, which also uses the channels that the file names. Without package specs, install_packages() does not warn about the channels in conda-meta/history. These abort before anything runs, with class condathis_install_packages_unsupported_definition (also condathis_invalid_arg):

  • A lock file, such as an @EXPLICIT or conda-lock file. It lists every package of an environment: create the environment again with create_env(env_definition(<file>), overwrite = TRUE).

  • A file that the backend cannot read, or a backend that cannot install from a file (also condathis_backend_unsupported).

Package specs and a definition together, or two definitions, abort with class condathis_install_packages_conflicting_args. A file that does not exist aborts with class condathis_install_packages_missing_env_file.

packages = <specs> still works. It is deprecated. It warns once per session (class condathis_deprecated_packages_arg) when the call comes from the console, a script or the tests of the package that makes it. Calls made inside other packages do not warn. packages = NULL and packages = character(0) install nothing and return status 0, as in 0.1.4.

Invalid specs abort with these classes:

  • condathis_install_packages_missing_packages: no specs and no env_definition(), unless packages = NULL or packages = character(0) was given.

  • condathis_install_packages_invalid_packages: a named argument that install_packages() does not have (the error names the closest argument; names are never abbreviated, so p = aborts too), a value that is not a character vector, NA or "", or a file name that ends in .yml, .yaml, .json or .lock (pass it with env_definition()).

  • condathis_install_packages_positional_env_name: env_name is not given, the specs are two or more unnamed arguments, and the last of them is one string that names an existing environment. Name the argument, as in env_name = "my-env". Specs given with packages = or as one vector are never checked this way.

  • condathis_install_packages_failed: the backend cannot read a spec, such as "::".

  • condathis_parse_match_spec_invalid_name (also condathis_invalid_arg): the same, when the conda-meta/history of the environment records channels, because condathis then reads the specs first.

  • condathis_parse_match_spec_invalid_url (also condathis_invalid_arg): the same, for the URL of a package file.

env_name

Character string with the environment name. It must be a plain directory name that is valid on Linux, macOS and Windows:

  • Not empty, and not . or ...

  • Not starting with -, and not ending with ..

  • Without path separators, :, #, whitespace, control characters or <>"|?*.

  • Not a Windows device name, such as NUL or COM1 (see Environment names in create_env()).

Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_env_name. run(), run_bin(), run_pipeline() and run_step() also accept an env_path() value. The other functions reject it with class condathis_env_path_read_only.

method

Character string naming the backend. "auto" (the default) uses the backend that owns env_name when it exists, and otherwise the first available backend in getOption("condathis.backend_priority") order (see condathis-options). Any name from list_registered_backend_names() selects that backend, and "micromamba" is built in. The name of a backend whose package condathis knows, such as "rattler" of the rattlerthis package, also selects it. condathis loads the package on first use. "native" is a deprecated alias for "micromamba" (warns once per session). The 0.1.4 default c("native", "auto") is read as "native".

If you name a backend other than the owner, functions that change the environment abort. The others warn and use the owner. The classes:

  • condathis_backend_not_installed: the package of the named backend is not installed.

  • condathis_backend_mismatch: the named backend does not own the environment, and the function changes it.

  • condathis_backend_mismatch_warning (a warning): the same, for a function that does not change the environment.

  • condathis_backend_ambiguous_env: several backends have an environment of that name, and method names none of them.

  • condathis_invalid_method: an invalid value.

verbose

Character string that controls the console output. One of:

  • "output": show the output of the command and the messages of condathis.

  • "silent": show nothing.

  • "cmd": show the command line.

  • "spinner": show only a spinner.

  • "full": show the command line, the output, and the backend's own log.

TRUE means "output" and FALSE means "silent". Every level except "silent" shows a spinner in interactive sessions. It also shows these messages and this warning when they occur (see condathis-conditions):

  • condathis_micromamba_downloading (a message): no usable micromamba was found, so it is downloaded. Queries, such as list_envs(), never download it.

  • condathis_env_lock_waiting and condathis_cache_lock_waiting (messages): the call waits for another R session.

  • condathis_install_micromamba_checksum_unavailable (a warning): the checksum of the downloaded micromamba could not be checked.

Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_verbose. The default is shown in Usage.

The command line shown, the cmd of a result and the messages of condathis show the password and the token of a URL as *****. micromamba does the same (https://user:*****@host/channel, https://host/t/*****/channel). The command still gets them.

channels

A non-empty character vector of channel names or URLs, in priority order. For a package from another channel, either name the channel in the spec ("bioconda::samtools") or add it here, as in channels = c("conda-forge", "bioconda"). Invalid values, such as NULL, NA or "", abort with class
condathis_install_packages_invalid_channels. condathis 0.1.4 also used "bioconda" by default. When channels is not given and the backend finds no package for a spec, the error says that the default changed.

The conda-meta/history of the environment records the channels of its packages. Pass each of them in channels or additional_channels. A channel named in a spec counts as passed. When the call leaves out one of them, install_packages() warns with class
condathis_install_packages_missing_previous_channels.

additional_channels

NULL (the default) or a non-empty character vector of channel names or URLs, used after channels. Invalid values abort with these classes:

  • condathis_install_packages_invalid_channels

  • condathis_invalid_additional_channels

channel_priority

Channel priority mode: "strict" (the default), "flexible" or "disabled", as in create_env(). Invalid values abort with class
condathis_install_packages_invalid_channel_priority.

Value

A condathis_result object, invisibly: a classed list with status, stdout, stderr, timeout, pid, cmd and env_name. cmd is the command line that the backend ran, or NA when the backend reports none. stdout, stderr and pid are NA when the backend reports none, and pid always is with micromamba. A backend failure aborts with class condathis_install_packages_failed (also condathis_backend_error), with the backend's error as the parent. micromamba runs the link scripts of packages. A backend that does not makes install_packages() warn with class condathis_install_packages_link_scripts_skipped (also condathis_link_scripts_skipped). The warning names the packages.

Details

install_packages() installs packages for the platform of the environment, with every backend. That platform is the one the environment was created for (see platform in create_env()). Otherwise, on Apple Silicon and on Windows, it is the platform of the environment's packages that are not noarch. An environment with no packages other than noarch ones, such as a new "condathis-env", gets the emulation fallback of create_env() instead. Packages that cannot be installed for the native platform then use an emulated platform, when they can be installed there. That platform is "osx-64" on Apple Silicon when Rosetta 2 is running. On Windows with a backend that solves for "win-arm64", such as the win-arm64 micromamba, it is "win-64". Later installs then use the same platform.

Other R sessions

Only one R session at a time changes an environment. create_env(), install_packages() and remove_env() hold a lock on the environment name while they work, with every backend. A call for an environment that another R session is changing waits until that session is done. After two seconds, the call says so with a message of class condathis_env_lock_waiting. verbose = "silent" hides this message. Ctrl-C stops the wait. clean_cache() waits until no other R session creates an environment or installs packages. Those calls wait while it cleans. Each wait gives a message of class condathis_cache_lock_waiting. A lock lasts only as long as its session, also when the session crashes or is killed. The lock files are in the directory locks of the condathis data directory (see get_install_dir()). Where files cannot be locked, such as on some network file systems, the call goes on without the lock. When it changes something, it warns once per session with class condathis_env_lock_unavailable.

See also

condathis-conditions for every condition class.

Other environments: create_env(), env_definition(), env_exists(), env_path(), get_env_dir(), list_envs(), list_packages(), remove_env(), validate_env()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
condathis::with_sandbox_dir({
  # A local channel shipped with condathis, with `polyglot`: a
  # dependency-free script that runs on Linux, macOS and Windows.
  channel <- system.file(
    "extdata", "polyglot-channel",
    package = "condathis"
  )

  # Install `polyglot` into an existing, empty environment.
  condathis::create_env(env_name = "my-env")
  condathis::install_packages(
    "polyglot",
    env_name = "my-env",
    channels = channel
  )

  condathis::create_env(
    "bioconda::fastqc",
    env_name = "fastqc-env"
  )
  # Add `python` to the `fastqc-env` environment, for scripts that read
  # the reports of `fastqc`. Keep unrelated tools in separate
  # environments, so that their dependencies cannot conflict.
  # `bioconda` is passed again, because `fastqc` came from it: leaving out
  # a channel the environment was built from warns. `conda-forge` comes
  # first: with strict channel priority, the first channel wins.
  condathis::install_packages(
    "python",
    env_name = "fastqc-env",
    channels = c("conda-forge", "bioconda")
  )
})
} # }
